key_insight: The paper proposes a hardware-agnostic three-layer architecture that standardizes fault-tolerant quantum computing by separating applications, fault-tolerance logic, and physical execution.
engineering_relevance: It provides a modular systems blueprint for building scalable, heterogeneous quantum stacks that can interface across devices, codes, and runtime control layers.
method: Defines three layers: application, fault-tolerance, and physical hardware.
Details five internal components of the Fault-Tolerance Layer and the data exchanged among them.
Maps execution, correction, and adaptation paths for logical synthesis, resource management, decoding, and runtime control.
evidence_signal: The abstract indicates the framework is validated through a full-stack end-to-end example illustrating the operating pipeline of fault-tolerant quantum algorithms.
watch_item: As a high-level abstract standard, the architecture still requires concrete mapping to specific hardware platforms, error-correction codes, and runtime implementations.
paper_title: A Three-Layer Architecture for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing
